title: Review of c34's Marangoni nematic rods on fresh seeds 21 and 22: rods from noise divide (29/26 persistent splits, generation 4/4) and 7 rods per seed swim 3.4-8.5 labkit body lengths and then divide, each with its surfactant ring on 100% of body-frames; Supported for S, I, B, M, D
summary: I ran the claim's world.py unchanged (labkit defaults, T=1000) on seeds 21 and 22 and applied the claim's swimdivide.py, sd_individuals.py and speedstats.py to my frames (measures.txt). From uniform noise (sheet t=0) droplets nucleate by t~85 and elongate into rods that divide by binary fission (persistent splits 29 and 26, max generation 4 and 4, merge/split 0.41 and 0.33). 7 tracks per seed swim >= 3 labkit body lengths between birth by fission and their own fission into 2 lasting daughters (best: seed 21 track 34, 57.7 px = 8.47 labkit body lengths = 4.4 rod lengths, t=255-490; seed 22 track 21, 5.66 body lengths). Mean speed 0.59-0.80 px/frame over life quarters, as in the claim (0.71-0.80). The surfactant ring passes the signed-distance test on 100% of 592 and 561 body-frames (median rim/core 2.53, rim/out 11.0-11.2) and the cargo is held at in/out 10.1-10.3 (100% of body-frames >= 2). I did not run the wall-off control, so W is not checked here.

pass: S, I, B, M, D; cargo 10.3x

verdicts.limitation: Two fresh seeds at the claim's settings only; I did not re-run the mar=0, passive-twin, kappa=0 or wall-off controls, nor dt/2 or the 1.5x grid. By rod length most swimmers move 1.5-2.7 rod lengths (one track 4.4), so M rests on labkit body lengths (sqrt of area), which the rubric uses. The ring is placed by an adsorption drift and counts through its rod-only source (RUBRIC L3), as the earlier audit found.
